task: Allow an operator to reassign a completed worker/subagent for follow-up work under an explicit worker role without using full-history fork.
outcome: After a worker finishes, the operator can run a follow-up command and see: "Worker reassignment ready" plus the previous dispatch id, new dispatch id, "mode: fresh-context", "role: <requested worker role>", a promptFile path, and nextAction text saying the worker can be started from explicit instructions with no full-history fork required.
facts: User clarified the pain point: after a subagent completes, they want to assign that agent more work, but the available full-history fork path cannot specify the worker role.
Existing dispatch commands already accept role on plan/prepare/run/auto, but dispatch_resume only resumes an existing dispatch id with the original selected host and no new role/objective arguments.
Existing dispatch records materialize prompt.md, worktree metadata, status/review output, workerIds for parallel workers, and role inside the handoff pack preview.
DispatchRecord already has an optional parentDispatchId field that can represent follow-up lineage.
The command registry supports adding dispatch_reassign through command-catalog, alias-normalizer, handler map, command-policy, DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS, and PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS.
constraints: Do not require or implement full conversation history inheritance.
Keep authority/receipt/DONE semantics unchanged; a reassignment is local dispatch metadata/worker guidance, not production acceptance.
Do not directly read or edit docs/story or tests/fixtures; use Lattice commands for story metadata and source/task smoke files for code verification.
Preserve existing dispatch_run, dispatch_resume, and dispatch_auto behavior unless the caller explicitly uses the reassignment path.
Because dispatch_reassign writes local dispatch metadata, register it in command-policy and process fact levels with L1 diagnostic-only semantics.
